title: A clinical study investigating whether it is safe to give children with newly diagnosed pontine diffuse midline glioma a drug called MTX110 using a device that helps deliver the drug directly to the tumour in the brain
official: A safety and feasibility study to investigate administration of intratumoral MTX110 via convection-enhanced delivery in children with newly diagnosed pontine diffuse midline glioma
summary:
Background and study aims 
Pontine diffuse midline glioma (DMG) is an extremely aggressive childhood brain tumour and is responsible for most brain tumour-related deaths in children. Most children survive for less than 1 year after diagnosis, and only around 10% survive beyond 2 years. These tumours develop deep within the brain, making surgical removal unsafe in most cases.
The current standard treatment is radiotherapy, which aims to shrink the tumour and relieve symptoms. However, radiotherapy is not curative and usually extends survival by only a few months. Standard chemotherapy has not been effective for DMG because the brain’s natural protective barriers, the blood–brain barrier (BBB) and blood–tumour barrier (BTB), prevent many drugs from reaching the tumour in sufficient amounts.
Previous studies have shown that it is feasible and safe to deliver drugs directly into the tumour, using an implantable device called the NeuroChase Drug Delivery System (NDDS). This device uses four very thin tubes, called catheters, which are carefully placed into the brain using detailed imaging to ensure accuracy. The tubes are connected to a ’port’ that sits on the skin surface. 
MTX110 is a new medicine that has shown promising results in an early clinical trial for children with DMG in the USA. In that study, doctors were able to find a dose that was both safe and potentially improved treatment, with children who received MTX110 directly into the tumour on average living longer than would usually be expected.
This study will investigate whether repeated doses of MTX110 delivered directly into the tumour after radiotherapy are safe and whether this approach may help children with newly diagnosed pontine DMG live longer. 

Who can participate? 
Patients age 3 to 16 years with DMG

What does the study involve? 
Participants will receive MTX110 infusions every 2–3 weeks until tumour progression.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating? 
Not provided at time of registration 

Where is the study run from? 
Cancer Research UK & UCL Cancer Trials Centre (UK)

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for? 
January 2027 to September 2032

Who is funding the study? 
Medical Research Council (UK)

Who is the main contact?
1. DELIVERY Trial Manager, ctc.DELIVERY@ucl.ac.uk
2. Dr Elwira Szychot, elwira.szychot@gosh.nhs.uk

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age ≥3 and ≤16 years at the time of diagnosis
2. Biopsy proven new diagnosis of H3K27M altered diffuse midline glioma (DMG) confined to the pons
3. Radiological diagnosis of pontine DMG (DIPG) confirmed by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), defined as tumours with a pontine location and diffuse involvement of at least 2/3 of the pons, based on diagnostic images before radiotherapy. 
4. No structural/anatomical changes cystic changes or hematoma obstructing the planned catheter trajectories identified on radiological images
5. Started focal radiotherapy by external beam to the brainstem as per local policy within 2-3 weeks from the time of diagnosis
6. Must be on a stable or decreasing dose of dexamethasone for at least 1 week prior to registration
7. Must be able to undergo MRI imaging with gadolinium based contrast administration (e.g., no ferrous-containing implants, no pacemakers etc) and a CT angiogram (with contrast) in order to facilitate surgical planning
8. No contraindications to neurosurgical implantation or general anaesthesia
9. Karnofsky Performance Status (age ≥ 10 years) or a Lansky Play Score of ≥50 assessed at diagnosis
10. Adequate renal function with glomerular filtration rate (GFR) ≥60 ml/min/1.73m2, based on a calculated method
11.	Adequate liver function:
11.1. Total bilirubin ≤2 × upper limit of normal (ULN) for age
11.2. Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) ≤2.5 × ULN for age 
12.	Adequate haematological function:
12.1. Haemoglobin ≥10 g/L (no transfusion within 7 days)
12.2. Peripheral absolute neutrophil count ≥1.5 x 10 9/L
12.3. Platelet count  ≥100 x 10 9/L (transfusion independent, defined as not receiving platelet transfusions for at least 7 days prior to   registration)
12.4. Normal coagulation defined as normal international normalized ratio (INR) or per institutional guidelines
13.	Participant and/or parent/legal guardian able to understand, and willing to sign, written informed consent 
14. Willing and able to participate in all required evaluations and procedures in the study protocol
15.	Negative serum or urine pregnancy test for women of childbearing potential (WOCBP) 
16. Willing to comply with the contraceptive requirements of the study
Exclusion criteria:
1. Radiological evidence of metastatic disease within the central nervous system (CNS) at diagnosis, including leptomeningeal or subarachnoid disseminated disease or other multifocal disease
2. Clinical and/or radiographic (MRI) progression of tumour following external beam radiation therapy
3. Unfavourable tumour morphology or the presence of a cavity or cysts that represent >50% of cross-sectional areas of the pons that may lead to poor convection-enhanced delivery (CED) coverage of a relevant part of the tumour. These participants should be discussed with the TMG
4. MRI or clinical evidence of uncontrolled tumour mass effect. The assessment of mass effect should be made by the treating team including neurosurgical input prior to any planned CED treatment
5. Untreated symptomatic hydrocephalus determined by the treating clinician
6. Non-correctable bleeding disorder
7. Signs of impending herniation or an acute intratumoral haemorrhage
8. Previous chemotherapy, investigational agents, biologic therapy, or other tumour-directed therapy for treatment of the tumour. Note: Radiotherapy as per inclusion criteria 5 and treatment directed at preventing or controlling oedema e.g. steroids before, during or after radiotherapy is allowed
9. History of allergic reactions or hypersensitivity attributed to compounds of similar chemical composition or pharmacological class to MTX110
10. Uncontrolled intercurrent illness including, but not limited to, ongoing or active infection, symptomatic heart failure, cardiac arrhythmia, or psychiatric illness/social situations, that could limit compliance with study requirements
11.	Systemic diseases which may be associated with unacceptable anaesthetic/operative risk
12.	History of seizures/epilepsy not well controlled on non-enzyme inducing anticonvulsant medication
13.	Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), hepatitis C virus antibody (anti-HCV) or human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) antibody positive
14. A device associated or other MRI artifact that would preclude planning or placement of the catheter system
15. Participants who in the opinion of the Investigator are unsuitable to participate
16. Life expectancy <12 weeks
